A small install.
A shorter test loop.

Clone the repo, run the installer, and keep coding. cfast uses an isolated Python environment and adds a command to ~/.local/bin/.

What you need
  • Linux and Python 3.10+
  • A C++20 capable g++
  • GNU time and prlimit
  • Git and internet for installation
Full installation guide

1. Install dependencies

Ubuntu / Debian
sudo apt install python3 python3-venv g++ git time util-linux

On another Linux distribution, install the equivalent packages.

2. Install cfast

mkdir -p ~/dev
git clone https://github.com/dhruvkshah75/cfast.git ~/dev/cfast
cd ~/dev/cfast
./install.sh

Keep this checkout in place. The installed command links to it.

3. Connect Competitive Companion

Install the browser extension, add 27121 in its Custom ports setting, then run cfast listen.

Getting “command not found”?

Add this line to your ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc, then open a new terminal:

export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

Small commands.
Useful control.

Use problem limits automatically, add a tricky case, or clear old downloads. The useful options are a command away.

Read the command guide
cfast 4A

Compile and check every saved case.

cfast 4A --timeout 2 --memory 256

Override CPU seconds and memory in MiB.

cfast 4A --eps 1e-6

Set an explicit floating point tolerance.

cfast --help

See every command, grouped by purpose.

Before your
first run.

A few things worth knowing.

Do I need to change my editor?

No. Write C++ in Sublime Text, Vim, VS Code, or any other editor. Save the file, then run cfast from a terminal in that directory. There is no editor plugin to install.

Does it match the Codeforces judge exactly?

cfast checks only the cases saved on your machine. It uses online-judge-tools for output comparison and Linux resource limits. Hidden tests, hardware, and memory accounting differ from Codeforces, so passing locally does not guarantee acceptance.

The memory ceiling applies to virtual address space, while reported peak RSS is resident memory. This can be stricter than the online judge. CPU limits also have whole second enforcement granularity, with a separate wall time guard.

Can I test without an internet connection?

Yes. After installation and importing samples, compilation and testing work offline. Reimporting samples needs access to the problem page and Competitive Companion.

Can I add my own tests and template?

Yes. Run cfast add 4A, or provide input and expected output files with --input and --output. Custom cases survive sample refreshes. Edit the repo’s template.cpp or put an override at ~/.cf/template.cpp. The supplied template reads a leading test count; adapt it for single case problems.

Will downloaded tests pile up forever?

Reimporting a problem replaces its downloaded samples. Run cfast clean to preview downloads unused for 30 days, then cfast clean --yes to remove them. A full reset with cfast clean --all --yes also deletes custom cases. Your solution files are outside the cache.

Which problems and languages are supported?

C++20 solutions on Linux, using standard input and output. Codeforces contest, problemset, and gym URLs are supported, including indexes such as B1. Interactive problems, file based I/O, and problems requiring a special checker are unsupported. Floating point tolerance is available with --eps.
